case_title: Jarnail Singh & Anr. v. State of Punjab
accused_occupation: Bus conductors of the Punjab Roadways depot
accused_victim_relationship: Co-worker (conductors allegedly acting in connivance with the General Manager)
evidence_type: Documentary (seized tickets, way-bills, enquiry report), recovery evidence, oral testimony of inspection team and checking officers
trial_court_outcome: Convicted the three conductors; three years rigorous imprisonment, Rs.1000 fine, six months additional in default. Four accused acquitted; eleven convicted in total
high_court_outcome: Appeal disposed; conviction of the three conductors confirmed; other accused acquitted
neutral_facts: A complaint by a bus driver of a state roadways depot alleged that the depot's general manager, in connivance with conductors and others, had been selling and using tickets printed on his own and sold through persons who collected money for him, causing large loss to the depot. Following the complaint, an inspection committee of three officers checked three buses on two routes on a given day. The inspectors took into possession old tickets, tickets whose value had been increased by affixing stamps, driver diaries and way-bills, and cash found in a conductor's ticket bag. The committee recorded statements of conductors, the general manager, a traffic manager and an assistant mechanical engineer, and prepared an enquiry report. Only a photocopy of that report was available. The seized tickets were later shown to two witnesses at a police station. None had been sealed, and tickets from the three buses were not segregated. Neither witness had been present at the recovery, and neither could say which tickets related to which bus. The inspection witnesses could not identify which conductor had been carrying which tickets. No passenger who had bought such tickets was examined. The prosecution case rested on these tickets and the inspection report.
financial_property_loss: Alleged loss of crores of rupees to the depot; not proved. Excess cash allegedly found at inspection was also not proved
motive: alleged: financial gain from selling self-printed tickets through persons who collected money for the general manager
key_evidence_accepted: None. The Court did not rely on the seized tickets or the enquiry report
witness_credibility: Court found PW-8 and PW-15 could not connect the tickets to the buses or the conductors; PW-20, PW-21 and PW-22 could not identify which accused had which tickets
bail_history: Already on bail at the Supreme Court stage; bail-bonds discharged
trial_duration: offence: 11.05.1996 (inspection; complaint dated 04.05.1996); trial judgment: 28.01.2002; High Court: 14.09.2009; Supreme Court: 12.07.2022
legal_representation: Appellants: Neeraj Kumar Jain, Sr. Adv., with D. P. Singh and others. State of Punjab: R. K. Rathore and Ms. Jaspreet Gogia
investigation_status: FIR registered; police report under s.173(2) CrPC filed; charges framed against 15 persons; 23 prosecution witnesses examined
procedural_irregularity: Enquiry report produced only as a photocopy; original's existence and loss not proved; State did not pursue secondary evidence; seized tickets not sealed or segregated
appeal_history: Trial court: 11 convicted, 4 acquitted. High Court: conviction of the three conductors confirmed, others acquitted. Supreme Court: appeals allowed and the three conductors acquitted
prosecution_argument: Conviction rests on reliable evidence; PW-8 and PW-15 proved recovery of tickets; PW-20, PW-21 and PW-22 proved inspection and enquiry report; appellants raise only technical objections
defence_argument: Enquiry report is a photocopy and only a fact-finding report; seized tickets unsealed and unsegregated; no passenger examined; excess cash not proved; no reliable evidence of guilt
legal_principle_applied: Recovery must be made in accordance with law and must link the seized material to the accused; secondary evidence requires proof of existence and loss of the original; charge must be proved by admissible evidence
precedent_relied_upon: Cited by appellants but not discussed by the Court: Ashok Dhulichand (1975) 4 SCC 664; Jai Dev AIR 1973 SC 612; Sharad Birdichand Sarda (1984) 4 SCC 116; Sujit Biswas (2013) 12 SCC 406; Samsul Haque (2019) 18 SCC 161; Sarwan Singh AIR 1957 SC 637; Shivaji S. Bobade (1973) 2 SCC 793; Subhash Chand (2002) 1 SCC 702; Rajiv Singh (2015) 16 SCC 369; State of U.P. v. Wasif Haider (2019) 2 SCC 303
other_sentence_order: Bail-bonds discharged; judgments of the High Court and trial court set aside qua the appellants
